relevance_note: Case report of a girl with Blau syndrome and a NOD2 variant inherited from her mother: "On genotyping of exon 4 of NOD2 a G464W substitution was found, confirming a diagnosis of Blau syndrome, with her mother demonstrating the same mutation".
method_note: Written by hand from a full reading; a small Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and checked spans and fields. Individuals: the case-report girl ('patient'), her mother (G464W carrier, affected per Figure 2 legend: recurrent fevers) and her father (tested, wild-type, unaffected). Siblings are mentioned only as 'Siblings were not tested' with no individual detail, so they get no rows. Literature persons from the Discussion with an individual-level feature were included: the ref 5 patient (stenosis of the primary branches of the aortic arch; Takayasu phenotype) and the ref 15 patient (isolated coronary sinus involvement, 'existing Blau phenotype'; no mutation analysis reported, so no variant row). Table 1 (published cases with Blau syndrome and large-vessel vasculitis) was converted as a single row whose cells hold several stacked values per column (counts '2/4 1 1 1 2 pedigrees', phenotypes, vascular phenotypes, mutation status, year/reference, familial/sporadic); under D-31 these were not assigned to references or people by position, so no rows were made from Table 1, and refs 11, 12, 13 (group statement 'involvement of the aorta and renal arteries 11,12,13') and ref 14 (2 families, 'no details are provided') get no rows. Table 2 lists mutations by reference only, without people. Variant G464W is printed as an amino-acid substitution without a 'p.' prefix; recorded in protein_hgvs_as_stated; no cDNA or transcript printed. Variant type 'missense' recorded from the authors' description 'A novel substitution, G464W' (amino-acid substitution). Zygosity is not stated. For the mother's variant row, type and pathogenicity are left 'not reported' (statements are about the proband's variant). Age at diagnosis not recorded: the clinical diagnosis was 'considered' at the age-8 presentation and the age at genetic confirmation is not given. Rash and uveitis exclusions come from the presentation at 18 months ('in the absence of rash, uveitis, or systemic features'); the later 'Her eye examination continued to be normal' was recorded only as 'abnormal eye examination' excluded (D-27). 'There were no systemic features' (age 8) is too broad to exclude a checklist item and was not recorded. Blood pressure was normal at the onset of the cardiac disease and hypertension was found 1.5 years later; these are different time points, not a contradiction, and only the later hypertension is recorded. 'Renal function has remained stable' was not taken as excluding renal failure. Inconsistencies in the paper: the text says 'We reported a similar case in 1989 5' while reference 5 and Table 1 give 1990; the introduction says 'We describe an 8-year-old girl' while the case report says 'now 11 years old' (8 years was the age at cardiac presentation); 'ejection fraction on electrocardiography' is printed where echocardiography seems meant.
